net_scope.note: The brainstorm's illustrative examples (vcc, +3V3, PWR_RTN) are present on the real board but are excluded from the plain A* pathfinder entirely by _should_route()'s power/ground/HV name-pattern matching -- handled by zone pours instead. This fix does not touch them; their disposition is unaffected by this change either way.

pre_fix_baseline.description: HV/AC-only fail-closed gate (docs/plans/2026-07-23-008), forced segments still allowed for every other net class

post_fix_measurement.description: Uniform fail-closed gate (this plan) -- no net class exempt from the forced-segment ban

delta.routed_nets: 72 -> 0 (every A*-routable net this test attempts was previously succeeding only via a fabricated forced segment; genuinely zero of the 84 A*-routable nets have a real, clearance-respecting path on this board today)
delta.solder_mask_bridge: 200 -> 57 (-143, downstream of far less copper being drawn)
delta.track_dangling_and_tracks_crossing_and_c: 19+34+1 -> 0 (categories disappear entirely -- no forced/dangling copper left to cause them)
delta.unconnected_items: 298 -> 326 (+28, expected: honestly-failed nets have no copper at all now)

verdict: Necessary and working as intended -- shorting_items and clearance violations both genuinely decreased, confirming the fix eliminates real fabricated-copper shorts rather than just hiding them. But the honest A*-routable completion rate on this specific board is 0%, not merely lower: pre-fix, all 72 of this test's 'successes' were forced segments. This is the true, previously-fabricated baseline this plan's R4/R5 anticipated -- more severe than illustrated, not different in kind. Re-routing the newly-honest 84 unrouted nets is explicitly out of scope for this plan (see Scope Boundaries) and is real, separate follow-up work: the plain A* engine on this board's current channel/grid setup essentially never finds a legal path without the escape hatch it used to lean on.
